messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted to the hospital after suffering syncope. On arrival, the patient was alert and showed impairments in speech fluency, comprehension, and repetition. Further examination revealed poor perfusion over the left middle cerebral artery. He was diagnosed with acute cerebral infarction with global aphasia and received a recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rtPA) injection. After 12 days of inpatient treatment, the patient was later discharged under stable conditions with global aphasia status and no focal neurologic signs.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course Summary:

The patient was admitted to the hospital after suffering syncope while playing tennis. The patient presented with global aphasia and impairments in audio comprehension and repetition. Brain CT with contrast revealed no apparent intracranial haemorrhage or mass, but CT perfusion indicated poor perfusion over the left middle cerebral territory. The patient diagnosed with acute cerebral infarction with global aphasia and received a recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rtPA) injection. Brain non-contrast MRI was conducted on day 5, revealing an acute infarction in the territory of the left middle cerebral artery, just in the perisylvian gyri. The patient was switched to the intensive care unit for further management. After 12 days of inpatient treatment, the patient was later discharged under stable conditions with global aphasia status and no focal neurologic signs. The patient then received speech rehabilitation, including verbal production, auditory comprehension training, augmentative communication training, phonetic placement, and high-level cognitive function training at two hospitals. The patient's language expression gradually recovered. The CCAT was then performed 14 months after the initial stroke.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is acute cerebral infarction in the left middle cerebral artery territory, confirmed on CT perfusion and MRI and treated with rtPA; the syncope was only the presenting symptom. This is a cerebrovascular disease, chapter I, category I63 (cerebral infarction).

CODE: I63
